newsitem.title: UK: London gold at lowest fix in almost four years.
newsitem.headline: London gold at lowest fix in almost four years.

text.p: Gold prices fell to their lowest fixing since April 22, 1993 as the bearish mood that has prevailed in the gold market for several months deepened on Friday.
Gold had closed in London on Thursday at $342.80/$343.30 an ounce but then met new pressure in New York and Tokyo.
It fixed in London on Friday at $340.90, down from Thursday's $342.80 fixing, and dealers forecast lower prices to come.
"The new target looks like the psychologically important $340.00 and then we are down to the low $330s," one dealer said as the price slithered southwards.

In contrast to gold, palladium prices reached their highest level in six months as users of the metal and speculators raided the spot market to counter shortages created by delayed 1997 export shipments from Russia to Japan, the main user of the metal.
Gold prices have been deteriorating for a year since they fixed at $416.25 in February 2 last year the highest since Feb 22, 1990.
But the trend accelerated since the middle of last year as gold producers stepped up selling to protect their income against falling prices.
At the same time, the suspicion grew that the central banks and other financial institutions were mulling selling gold from their reserves.
All this year rumoured sales by European central banks have flattened market sentiment which was not improved by confirmation that the Dutch central bank had sold 300 tonnes from reserves.
"The factors for gold are the same as we have seen all year but I am more convinced that central banks have been in the market and selling," one dealer based in continental Europe said.
Further the dealer said he was seeing selling by "desperate" investors who had bought at "remarkably higher prices" years ago and were realising that these would not be seen again in the medium term.
Dealers also noted that the gold producers were still actively hedging to protect themselves against falling prices.
Dealer opinion varied on the level of physical demand for gold. Some said it was holding up reasonably well but not in bulk enough to turn the price round.
Others argued that demand in the Middle and Far East had slowed and the strong U.S. dollar was making gold unattractive to potential European investors.
"The high dollar against the mark is making it (investing in gold) much harder," one dealer said.
Palladium was fixed at $130.50, $1.50 up since Thursday.

"Palladium is the only one (of the precious metals) which is higher now than at the start of the year and that is down to the delayed Russian shipments driving end users into the market," a dealer said.
Its sister metal platinum was a little easier at $349.75/$350.75 down $1.50 but had also benefitted from, the Russia-Japan problem.
Silver was a cent lower at $4.81/$4.82.
